initial_requirements: Project ZNIX aims to provide an object-based, application-independent framework for retrieving and manipulating personal information. Casual users should be able to archive diverse information, organize it through relationships and hierarchies they find meaningful, and add, change, remove, categorize, or back up items without disrupting that organization. The framework should also expose services that allow compatible client applications to work with the same information.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary goals ZNIX must achieve for its different stakeholder roles—for example, end users, client application developers, and administrators—and how should success be defined for each?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
For end users, the main goal is to keep personal information organized in a way that makes sense to them, without losing that structure when they add, edit, delete, or back things up. Success there would mean they can retrieve and manage their information easily across different kinds of content, and the relationships they create stay intact over time.
For client application developers, the goal is to have a stable, application-independent framework they can plug into so their apps can work with the same underlying information. Success would mean the API or services are reliable, consistent, and let their applications access and manipulate data without needing to invent their own storage model.
For administrators or support staff, the goal is usually to keep the system dependable, safe, and maintainable. I’d say success for them is measured by smooth backups and recovery, low data loss risk, good performance, and being able to support multiple clients or users without the framework becoming fragile or hard to manage.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: End users should be able to organize personal information in a way that makes sense to them and preserve that structure when adding, editing, deleting, or backing up items. Client application developers need a stable, application-independent framework and reliable services/API so their apps can work with the same underlying information. Administrators or support staff need the system to be dependable, safe, maintainable, support smooth backup/recovery, minimize data loss risk, and handle multiple clients or users without becoming fragile.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: End users; client application developers; administrators/support staff.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: Archive diverse personal information; organize items using user-defined relationships and hierarchies; add, change, remove, and categorize items; back up items without disrupting organization; expose services/API for compatible client applications to access and manipulate the same information.

slots.name: business_rules
slots.value: User-created organizational structure and relationships must remain intact when information is added, edited, deleted, or backed up. The framework should remain application-independent so different clients can share the same underlying information model.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Personal information items of diverse content types; relationships between items; hierarchies/organizational structures; backup copies; shared underlying information accessible by client applications.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: Must be application-independent; must support compatible client applications using the same underlying information; must preserve organization during modification and backup operations.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: Reliability, consistency, maintainability, dependability, safety, smooth backup and recovery, low data-loss risk, and good performance.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: System should handle add/edit/delete/backup operations without disrupting organization; support multiple clients or users without becoming fragile or hard to manage; preserve relationships and hierarchies over time.
